chapter_theme: The sun of knowledge (ஞானாதித்தன்): bindu and nada dawn within the heart as the source of the kalas and of speech, and the Lord is a light beyond sun, moon and fire, travelling through all the worlds, shining at centres in the body, and removing a darkness the outer lights cannot.
structure_note: Two verses on bindu and nada as an inner dawn (1993, 1994), one on the Lord's titles (1995), then verses on his light within (1996 to 2000).

1993.reading: Bindu spread into two, lower and higher; the lower became the higher nada, and with the higher kala and the rest set within them they rise in the heart like the dawn.
1993.nuance: அபரம், பரம் (lower, higher) and பரநாதம் are terms of Siddhanta cosmology. அருணோதயம் (sunrise) gives the chapter its sun: the unfolding of bindu is pictured as an inner dawn.

1994.reading: The sound that rises at that inner dawn is the working of clear higher nada, so the bounteous higher bindu and the speech that begins with vaikhari are one rising for the five kalas.
1994.nuance: வைகரி is the spoken level of speech, traditionally the last of four (with madhyama, pashyanti and sukshma). ஐங்கலை are taken as the five kalas beginning with nivritti. The verse ties sound and speech back to one source.

1995.reading: The celestials say he is the Lord of the gods who rises in the ten directions, who of old was called Lord of the three, the Lord of the four who goes on teaching from the centre, the Lord who abides.
1995.nuance: மூவர் are traditionally Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, and நால்வர் the four sages taught by Siva as Dakshinamurti; நடுவாய் உரையாநிற்கும் may refer to that teaching. Neither identification is in the verse.

1996.reading: My father, without falsehood and true, lord of the worlds: moon, fire and sun remove the black darkness, but Nandi, holy one who removes the darkness that deeds make, rose mingled in me so that the darkness close at hand left.
1996.nuance: The contrast is between outer lights and the inner one. செய்யிருள் (darkness of deeds, or dense darkness) and கையிருள் (darkness at hand, or within one's grasp) are both open; tradition takes the inner darkness as the soul's impurity.

1997.reading: Lighting the single flame so that the wavering darkness leaves, the juice of the rare fruit above comes near; and that is also the form of the great flame the Lord of Kailash, who stands as a ripened flame, took on above.
1997.nuance: மேலை அருங்கனி ஊறல் (the juice of the rare fruit above) is commonly read as the nectar said to flow from the head in yoga, and கயிலை as the crown of the head. அனித்திடும் is obscure. The verse is compressed and the reading is a guess at its order.

1998.reading: The great light that fills as true knowledge goes to and returns from the worlds without strife, and becomes the light of a quarter no chariot knows; who knows this? It is the Lord.
1998.nuance: தேரறியாத may be 'that no chariot knows', the sun's chariot not reaching it, so a light beyond the sun; or 'that inquiry cannot know', from தேர் (to examine). Both readings stand.

1999.reading: The sun that blossoms within the circle becomes the light of rays within the region; going out it travels to all eight directions, and for those who know rightly it stays in its place.
1999.nuance: மண்டலம் and கண்டிதம் are probably regions of the yogic body (கண்டம் may be the throat), but the verse does not fix them. The contrast is between the light going out everywhere and standing still for the one who knows.

2000.reading: They perceived the flame that shines in five places, the navel, the nose, the eyes, their middle and the crown, as the three: the Lord of the gods, Tirumal and Brahma.
2000.nuance: The five places are centres of contemplation; நாசி நயன நடுவு may be one place, between nose and eyes, and தூபி the crown of the head. Who perceives (the gods, or the sages) is not clear in the verse.

links.note: 1923 lists what comes from bindu; 1993 divides bindu into lower and higher and pictures the unfolding as a dawn in the heart, setting up the chapter's sun of knowledge.
